title: Lord, I Esteem Thy Judgments Right
description: Lord, I Esteem Thy Judgments Right in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 6, headed “Holiness and comfort from the word”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, I es-teem thy judg-ments right, And all thy sta-tutes just; Thence I main-tain a con-stant fight With ev-ery flat-tering lust.

lines: Lord, I esteem thy judgments right,
Thence I maintain a constant fight
I keep thy law in sight,
Thro' all the business of the day,
My heart in midnight silence cries,
My thoughts in holy wonder rise,
And bring their thanks to thee.
And when my spirit drinks her fill
At some good word of thine,
Not mighty men that share the spoil

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
